applicable_when: The kernel is a 4D tensor layout permutation (channels-last to contiguous). The load address is y0 + 128*x2 + 4032000*y1: consecutive threads vary x2, so consecutive load addresses differ by 128 bytes (stride-128). This means 32 threads in a warp touch 32x128=4096 bytes spread across 128 cache sectors instead of 1 — catastrophically non-coalesced loads. L2 is saturated at 97.13%, L1 hit rate is 0%, and 80.26% of scheduler cycles have no eligible warp due to L1TEX stalls averaging 42.4 cycles. Stores (x2 + 31500*y3) are contiguous in x2 and therefore already coalesced. The fix is a shared-memory transpose tile using tl.trans: load a [YBLOCK x XBLOCK] tile coalesced along y (stride-1 in source), transpose in registers/smem via tl.trans, then store coalesced along x (stride-1 in destination). This converts the stride-128 global load into coalesced loads + register transpose + coalesced stores, dramatically reducing L2 sector traffic.
